info.name: TileFX
info.comment: A filter effect that repeats its input to fill the primitive subregion.

description.p: TileFX takes the primitive subregion of its FilterEffect.Input as a tile and repeats it across its own primitive subregion, as for the SVG feTile element. The tile lattice is anchored at the top-left of the input's subregion, so the tile appears at its original position and the copies extend from it in every direction.

The input's subregion is typically set with FilterEffect.X, FilterEffect.Y, FilterEffect.Width and FilterEffect.Height on the producer, e.g. a FloodFX or OffsetFX limited to a small rectangle. A standard source such as SourceGraphic covers the filter region, so tiling it has no visible effect.

Unlike other effects, the default primitive subregion of a TileFX is the full filter region rather than the subregion of its input, so that a TileFX without an explicit subregion fills the filter region.

The result has the same data kind as the input. Colour images are copied without colour conversion, so a tiled normal map produced by a LightingFX of type NORMAL is still recognised as a normal map. Scalar heights produced in the HEIGHT output mode of TurbulenceFX or BlurFX remain floating-point values, so they can be tiled at full precision before they are lit.

If the tile covers a whole number of device pixels, every pixel of the output is an exact copy of a pixel in the tile. Otherwise, for example when the client is scaled or rotated, the tile is resampled with bilinear interpolation. Interpolation wraps across the edges of the tile, so the copies join without seams. Repetition does not repair discontinuities that are already present between opposite edges of the tile.

action.name: Draw
action.comment: Draws object graphics to drawable areas.
action.prototype: ERR acDraw(*Object, DOUBLE X, DOUBLE Y, DOUBLE Width, DOUBLE Height)

input.param: The X position of the region to be drawn.
The Y position of the region to be drawn.
The width of the region to be drawn.
The height of the region to be drawn.

field.name: XMLDef
field.comment: Returns an SVG compliant XML string that describes the effect.
